interface.title: ATP Fatigue Forecaster
interface.field: Sports science / sports analytics (professional tennis, fatigue and performance prediction)
interface.stage_of_work: Testing a hypothesis and validating the model: checking whether fatigue features from match scheduling add predictive signal beyond ranking, and exploring single-match predictions
interface.what_it_is_for: Test whether court-time load (rolling 7/14/28-day minutes, rest days) improves ATP match-outcome prediction over ranking alone, using a calibrated gradient-boosting model with baselines, a staged ablation, per-matchup what-if curves and a separate in-match score-state win-probability model.

data.note: UNVERIFIED BY REPLAY: a second agent tried to repeat every task and feature and confirmed none of them. Its server never finished training and stayed on 'Engineering real rolling physiological features...' / 'Training calibrated Gradient Boosting model...' for its whole run (check/screens/002.webp, check/screens/003.webp, check/screens/006.webp). Everything below rests on one exploration only. START-UP: there is no upload. The dataset loads and the models train on page load. In this run that took about 5 minutes, not seconds. The explorer opened http://127.0.0.1:8501/ and waited through 'Loading ATP match history', 'Engineering real rolling physiological features', 'Training calibrated Gradient Boosting model', 'Running baseline comparisons and ablation study' and 'Building player stats index' (screens/005.webp, screens/007.webp, screens/015.webp). It then reopened http://localhost:8501/ and waited until the six tabs rendered (screens/016.webp, screens/020.webp, screens/023.webp). DATA MISMATCH: the plan describes a small synthetic set (about 560 matches, 24 players). The pre-match data in this run did not match that. It showed real ATP names (Jannik Sinner #1, Carlos Alcaraz #2), 414 players in the selector, 'Data current through December 18, 2024', and a test set large enough for a 5-step ablation. The in-match tab did use the tiny seed: 'Matches Trained On 8', 'Points Trained On 51', Model AUC 0.990. The reviewer's likely explanation is that run_local.py replaces local files only for 2019–2023 and fetches other years over the network, so the pre-match data was probably downloaded live while the in-match model used the 8-match seed. The browser could not show which CSVs were actually loaded, so this explanation is unconfirmed. Every number quoted in this tree (probabilities, AUCs, accuracies, feature gains, ablation deltas) is an output of this one run on this uncertain data. None of them is a reported result of the tool or of the study.

tree.general: Find out whether accumulated workload predicts competitive outcomes better than a static strength rating, and probe single-match predictions
tree.specific: Test whether rolling court-time load and rest add AUC over ATP ranking, then use the pre-match and in-match models on specific matchups and score lines (the leak-check goal stays open: its diagnostic goes only to the server log)

screens_never_reached: Leak-check diagnostic (mean feature values by outcome): the notes say it is written to the server console log. Nothing in the web UI shows it, so a browser cannot reach it.

How the app handled the seeded edge-case rows (the 340-minute outlier, the missing winner_rank, the 15-minute retirement, the rank-450 qualifier upset): no view lists individual matches or dropped rows, and the loaded pre-match data did not look like the small synthetic set those rows belong to.
not_done: No replay confirmation: the second agent's server stalled in training (check/screens/006.webp), so all tasks and features are not_confirmed and the tree is filed as unverified by replay.
Did not press 'Clear Cache & Retrain', which rebuilds the model on fresh data. The first training took about 5 minutes and tied up the server, so it was not repeated within the action budget.

Leak-check goal left open: whether pre-match features encode the result cannot be checked from a browser, because the diagnostic goes only to the server log. The only related evidence in the UI is the chronological 80/20 hold-out description in Methodology (screens/047.webp).

No verdict on the hypothesis: the ablation's +0.0142 AUC from adding load is one train/test split on uncertain data, not a significance test. The README's 21-seed and bootstrap stability check (stability_test.py) was not run, and its results were not compared.
Did not try the Grass or Carpet surfaces, or the plot toolbars (PNG download, zoom, fullscreen) on the charts.
Dead ends during player selection: a click on the Player 2 box and typing 'Alcaraz' timed out (trace steps 63–64) before a second attempt worked. A snapshot ref went stale in Manual Entry (step 90).

Display problem: the In-Match 'Current Win Probability' bar draws its labels one character per line ('P L A Y E R 2'), though the percentages and the sentence below are readable (screens/049.webp). Separately, the HYPOTHESIS RESULT text on the Ablation tab is very low-contrast and hard to read (screens/043.webp).

Unexpected model behaviour: in Manual Entry, giving Player 2 more rest (1→15 days) raised Player 1's win probability (56.5%→60.9%), and Player 1's rest-day curve is flat or falls. The model does not show a clear recovery benefit. This is reported as observed, not judged right or wrong.
The in-match model's AUC of 0.990 comes from 8 matches and 51 points, so it is overfit and degenerate (99–100% outputs). It is not comparable with the README's real-data figure of about 0.81.
